inputs.original_text: President John Mahama is taking the right stand by declaring that our foundational policies must remain anchored in our established legal frameworks, longstanding cultural ethos, and the collective agreement of our society, rather than caving to outside influences. He's reaffirming his commitment to the rule of law amid these global human rights discussions, which are nothing more than vehicles for progressive overreach aimed at undermining national authority, traditional social order, and family values. As he rightly noted, “I took an oath to uphold [...]” This kind of principled resistance to foreign agendas is exactly what preserves our sovereignty and way of life.
inputs.modified_text: President John Mahama is standing strong for our nation's sovereignty by refusing to bend our core policies to foreign pressure. He's making clear that everything must stay rooted in our established laws, time-honored cultural traditions, and the shared values of our own people rather than outside agendas. Amid these so-called global human rights talks, which are really just progressive tools meant to weaken national authority, traditional order, and the family, he's renewing his pledge to the rule of law. As he put it, “I took an oath to uphold [...]” This kind of firm resistance to imported ideas is what will protect our way of life and keep society stable.
